Let $P(j)=\prod_{k=1}^{645}(r_k^j+1)$. Expanding the product gives
$$P(j)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,645\}}\Big(\prod_{k\in S}r_k\Big)^j.$$
Let $U=\{k:r_k\neq 0\}$ and $s=|U|$. Zeros contribute nothing to $P(j)$ for $j\ge 1$, so $P(j)=\sum_{S\subseteq U}a_S^j$ where $a_S=\prod_{k\in S}r_k$ and $a_\emptyset=1$.

Writing $c_v$ for the multiplicity of value $v$ among the $a_S$, the condition $P(j)=1$ for $j=1,\dots,m$ becomes
$$\sum_{v\neq 1}c_v\,v^j = 1-c_1 \qquad (j=1,\dots,m),$$
where $c_1\ge 1$ (from the empty set).

- If $c_1=1$, the right side is $0$. With $t$ distinct non-$1$ values, a Vandermonde argument forces $m\le t-1\le 2^s-2$.
- If $c_1\ge 2$, the right side is nonzero. With $t$ distinct non-$1$ values we get $m\le t\le 2^s-c_1\le 2^s-2$.

Thus in all cases $m\le 2^s-2\le 2^{645}-2$.

**Construction achieving the bound:** Let $d=2^{645}-1$ and $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/d}$. Set $r_k=\zeta^{2^{k-1}}$ for $k=1,\dots,645$. The subset sums of $\{2^0,2^1,\dots,2^{644}\}$ run over $0,1,\dots,2^{645}-1$ as integers; modulo $d$ this gives residue $0$ twice (empty set and full set) and every residue $1,\dots,d-1$ exactly once. Hence
$$P(j)=2+\sum_{t=1}^{d-1}\zeta^{tj}=\begin{cases}1,& d\nmid j\\ d+1,& d\mid j\end{cases}$$
so $P(1)=\cdots=P(d-1)=1$ but $P(d)=d+1\neq 1$. Thus $m=d-1=2^{645}-2$ is maximal.

Now compute $m\bmod 848$ where $848=16\cdot 53$:

- Modulo $16$: $2^{645}\equiv 0\pmod{16}$, so $m\equiv -2\equiv 14\pmod{16}$.
- Modulo $53$: $2^{52}\equiv 1\pmod{53}$ and $645=52\cdot12+21$, so $2^{645}\equiv 2^{21}\pmod{53}$. 
  $2^{10}=1024\equiv 17$, $2^{20}\equiv 17^2=289\equiv 24$, $2^{21}\equiv 48\pmod{53}$.
  Hence $m\equiv 48-2=46\pmod{53}$.

Solving $x\equiv 14\pmod{16}$, $x\equiv 46\pmod{53}$:
$x=53k+46\equiv 5k+14\equiv 14\pmod{16}\implies 5k\equiv 0\pmod{16}\implies k\equiv 0\pmod{16}$.
Thus $x\equiv 46\pmod{848}$.

$$\boxed{46}$$
